metadata.title: Sinkhorn Distances: Lightspeed Computation of Optimal Transportation Distances
metadata.note: Worked-example gold annotation, NOT part of the 10-paper Benchmark-1 evaluation set. Iteratively curated from silver Opus scaffold; differences against silver report as the silver-vs-gold agreement metric.

nodes.name: Probability Simplex
nodes.statement: The simplex $\Sigma_d \defeq \{x \in \mathbb{R}^d_+ : x^T \mathbf{1}_d = 1\}$ is the set of $d$-dimensional probability vectors (histograms).
nodes.statement_clean: The set of d-dimensional probability vectors summing to 1.

nodes.name: Transportation Polytope
nodes.statement: For $r, c \in \Sigma_d$, the transportation polytope is $U(r,c) \defeq \{P \in \mathbb{R}_+^{d \times d} \mid P\mathbf{1}_d = r,\, P^T\mathbf{1}_d = c\}$ — the set of joint probabilities with marginals $r$ and $c$.
nodes.statement_clean: The set of nonnegative d-by-d matrices with row sums r and column sums c.

nodes.name: Entropy and Kullback-Leibler Divergence
nodes.statement: For $r \in \Sigma_d$, $h(r) = -\sum_{i=1}^d r_i \log r_i$; for $P \in U(r,c)$, $h(P) = -\sum_{i,j} p_{ij} \log p_{ij}$; and $\mathbf{KL}(P\|Q) = \sum_{ij} p_{ij} \log(p_{ij}/q_{ij})$.
nodes.statement_clean: Standard Shannon entropy for marginals and joint tables, plus the KL divergence between two tables.

nodes.name: Cone of Distance Matrices
nodes.statement: $\mathcal{M} = \{M \in \mathbb{R}_+^{d\times d} : \forall i, m_{ii}=0;\ \forall i,j,k,\ m_{ij} \leq m_{ik} + m_{kj}\}$ is the cone of (pseudo-)metric matrices on $\{1,\ldots,d\}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Nonnegative symmetric matrices with zero diagonal satisfying the triangle inequality.

nodes.name: Optimal Transportation Problem
nodes.statement: Given a $d\times d$ cost matrix $M$ and marginals $r,c \in \Sigma_d$, compute $d_M(r,c) \defeq \min_{P \in U(r,c)} \langle P, M \rangle$.
nodes.statement_clean: Minimize the Frobenius inner product between a transportation plan P and a cost matrix M over the transportation polytope.

nodes.name: Basic Entropy Inequality for Joint Probabilities
nodes.statement: $\forall r, c \in \Sigma_d,\ \forall P \in U(r,c),\ h(P) \leq h(r) + h(c)$, with equality at the independence table $P = rc^T$.
nodes.statement_clean: The entropy of any joint distribution is bounded by the sum of its marginal entropies, with equality at the product table.
nodes.origin_citation: Cover & Thomas, Elements of Information Theory, Sec. 2

nodes.name: Entropy-Constrained Transportation Polytope
nodes.statement: For $\alpha \geq 0$, $U_\alpha(r,c) \defeq \{P \in U(r,c) \mid \mathbf{KL}(P \| rc^T) \leq \alpha\} = \{P \in U(r,c) \mid h(P) \geq h(r)+h(c)-\alpha\}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Subset of U(r,c) consisting of joint tables with KL distance at most alpha from the independence table.

nodes.name: Sinkhorn Distance
nodes.statement: $d_{M,\alpha}(r,c) \defeq \min_{P \in U_\alpha(r,c)} \langle P, M \rangle$ — the optimal transportation cost over the entropy-constrained polytope.
nodes.statement_clean: Optimal transport cost over the entropy-restricted transportation polytope.

nodes.name: Sinkhorn Reduces to Optimal Transport for Large $\alpha$
nodes.statement: For $\alpha$ large enough, the Sinkhorn distance $d_{M,\alpha}$ coincides with the classical transportation distance $d_M$.
nodes.statement_clean: When the entropic budget alpha is large enough, the Sinkhorn distance equals the classical optimal transport distance.

nodes.name: Independence Kernel
nodes.statement: When $\alpha = 0$ and $M$ is a Euclidean distance matrix, $d_{M,0}(r,c) = r^T M c$ is a negative-definite kernel; equivalently $e^{-t\, r^T M c}$ is positive-definite for all $t>0$.
nodes.statement_clean: At alpha=0 with Euclidean M, the Sinkhorn distance reduces to r^T M c, which is negative-definite.

nodes.name: Sinkhorn Distances Are Symmetric and Satisfy Triangle Inequality
nodes.statement: For all $\alpha \geq 0$ and $M \in \mathcal{M}$, $d_{M,\alpha}$ is symmetric and satisfies all triangle inequalities. The function $(r,c) \mapsto \mathbf{1}_{r \neq c}\, d_{M,\alpha}(r,c)$ satisfies all three distance axioms.
nodes.statement_clean: Sinkhorn distances are symmetric and obey the triangle inequality; multiplying by an indicator recovers the coincidence axiom.

nodes.name: Gluing Lemma With Entropic Constraint
nodes.statement: Let $\alpha \geq 0$ and $x,y,z \in \Sigma_d$. Given $P \in U_\alpha(x,y)$ and $Q \in U_\alpha(y,z)$, the matrix $S$ with $s_{ik} \defeq \sum_j p_{ij} q_{jk}/y_j$ satisfies $S \in U_\alpha(x,z)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Two entropy-constrained joint tables (P on x,y and Q on y,z) can be glued via the y-conditional product to produce an entropy-constrained joint table on (x,z).

nodes.name: Sinkhorn's Matrix-Scaling Theorem
nodes.statement: Given a positive matrix $K = e^{-\lambda M}$ and marginals $r, c$, there exist unique (up to scaling) positive vectors $u, v$ such that $P^\lambda = \mathrm{diag}(u)\, K\, \mathrm{diag}(v)$ has row sums $r$ and column sums $c$.
nodes.statement_clean: A unique diagonal scaling of a positive matrix realizes any prescribed positive row and column sums.

nodes.name: Equality Condition in the Marginal Entropy Bound
nodes.statement: For $P \in U(r,c)$, equality $h(P) = h(r) + h(c)$ holds if and only if $P = rc^T$.
nodes.statement_clean: Joint entropy equals the sum of marginal entropies precisely when the joint is the product of its marginals.

nodes.name: Data Processing Inequality
nodes.statement: If $X \to Y \to Z$ is a Markov chain, then $I(X;Y) \geq I(X;Z)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Mutual information cannot increase along a Markov chain.

nodes.name: Network Simplex Method for Optimal Transportation
nodes.statement: Combinatorial LP solver computing the classical optimal transportation cost $d_M(r,c)$ with worst-case complexity $O(d^3 \log d)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Classical LP solver for optimal transportation with super-cubic cost.

nodes.name: Dual-Sinkhorn Divergence
nodes.statement: $d_M^\lambda(r,c) \defeq \langle P^\lambda, M\rangle$, where $P^\lambda = \arg\min_{P \in U(r,c)} \langle P, M\rangle - \frac{1}{\lambda} h(P)$. By duality, for each $\alpha$ there is a $\lambda \in [0,\infty]$ with $d_{M,\alpha} = d_M^\lambda$.
nodes.statement_clean: Lagrangian (entropically regularized) form of the Sinkhorn distance with multiplier 1/lambda.

nodes.name: Sinkhorn-Knopp Algorithm
nodes.statement: Iterative matrix-scaling algorithm that computes the dual-Sinkhorn divergence $d_M^\lambda(r,c)$ via fixed-point iteration on the scaling vectors $u, v$.
output: Scaling vectors $u, v$ such that $P^\lambda = \mathrm{diag}(u)\, K\, \mathrm{diag}(v)$
nodes.pseudocode: I = (r>0); r = r(I); M = M(I,:); K = exp(-lambda*M); x = ones(length(r),size(c,2))/length(r); while x changes do x = diag(1./r)*K*(c.*(1./(K'*(1./x)))); end; u = 1./x; v = c.*(1./(K'*u)); d_M^lambda(r,c) = sum(u.*((K.*M)*v))

nodes.name: Proof of Property 1 (large-$\alpha$ equivalence)
nodes.statement: Since $h(P) \geq \tfrac12(h(r)+h(c))$ for any $P \in U(r,c)$, for $t$ large enough $U_t(r,c) = U(r,c)$, so $d_{M,t} = d_M$.

nodes.name: Proof of Property 2 (Independence Kernel)
nodes.statement: When $\alpha=0$, $U_0(r,c) = \{rc^T\}$ by Theorem 2.6.6 of Cover & Thomas, so $d_{M,0}(r,c) = r^T M c$. Expanding $m_{ij} = \|\varphi_i - \varphi_j\|^2$ shows $r^T M c$ is a sum of negative-definite kernels.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1 (metric properties)
nodes.statement: Symmetry follows from $M$'s symmetry. For the triangle inequality, glue optimal $P \in U_\alpha(x,y)$ and $Q \in U_\alpha(y,z)$ via Lemma 1 to obtain $S \in U_\alpha(x,z)$ and bound $\langle S, M\rangle$ using $m_{ik} \leq m_{ij}+m_{jk}$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 1 (Gluing Lemma)
nodes.statement: Define $T$ on $\{1,\ldots,d\}^3$ by $t_{ijk} = p_{ij}q_{jk}/y_j$ (and 0 when $y_j=0$); show $S = \sum_j T$ has marginals $x$ and $z$; then use the data processing inequality on the Markov chain $X \to Y \to Z$ to get $h(S) \geq h(x)+h(z)-\alpha$.

nodes.name: Faster Independence Kernel via Cholesky Preprocessing
nodes.statement: Pre-compute the norm vector $u$ and a Cholesky factor $L$ of the Gram matrix $K$; replace each histogram $r_i$ by $L r_i$ and store $r_i^T u$ to evaluate the Independence kernel quickly. The kernel is positive-definite on histograms with the same 1-norm but not on arbitrary vectors.

nodes.name: MNIST Digits Classification
nodes.statement: Classify MNIST digits (each treated as a normalized histogram on a $20\times 20$ pixel grid) using SVMs with kernel $e^{-d/t}$, varying $N \in \{3,5,12,17,25\}\times 10^3$. Sinkhorn distance with $\lambda=9$ outperforms EMD, Hellinger, $\chi^2$, Total Variation, and Gaussian.

nodes.name: Convergence of Sinkhorn Distance to EMD
nodes.statement: Boxplot of $(d_M^\lambda(r,c) - d_M(r,c))/d_M(r,c)$ over $40^2$ MNIST pairs as $\lambda$ grows; even for large $\lambda$, Sinkhorn hovers about 10\% above EMD.

nodes.name: Computational Speed Comparison
nodes.statement: Benchmark Sinkhorn (CPU and GPU) vs. Rubner's and Pele-Werman's EMD implementations on uniformly-sampled simplex points with random distance matrices. Sinkhorn is over $10^5$ times faster than EMD solvers at large $d$ with tolerance $0.01$; GPU adds another order of magnitude.

nodes.name: Empirical Iteration-Count Complexity
nodes.statement: Replicates the speed experiment focusing on the number of Sinkhorn-Knopp iterations needed for $\|x - x'\|_2 \leq 0.01$; iteration count grows as $e^{-\lambda M}$ becomes diagonally dominant.

nodes.name: Drop zero-marginal entries and form kernel $K$
nodes.statement: Set $I = (r>0)$, restrict $r$ and $M$ to indices $I$, then form the Gibbs kernel $K = \exp(-\lambda M)$.

nodes.name: Initialize scaling vector $x$
nodes.statement: Set $x = \mathbf{1}/|r|$, a uniform vector of length $|r|$ (or matrix-shaped if $c$ is a column family $C$).

nodes.name: Sinkhorn fixed-point loop
nodes.statement: While $x$ changes, update $x \leftarrow \mathrm{diag}(1/r)\, K\, (c .* (1/(K^T (1/x))))$ — one combined row/column rescaling per iteration.

nodes.name: Recover scaling vectors $u, v$
nodes.statement: After convergence set $u = 1/x$ and $v = c .* (1/(K^T u))$ so that $P^\lambda = \mathrm{diag}(u)\, K\, \mathrm{diag}(v)$.

nodes.name: Return dual-Sinkhorn divergence
nodes.statement: Return $d_M^\lambda(r,c) = \sum (u .* ((K .* M)\, v)) = \langle P^\lambda, M\rangle$.

nodes.name: Symmetry of $d_{M,\alpha}$
nodes.statement: Symmetry of $d_{M,\alpha}$ follows directly from the symmetry of the cost matrix $M$ and the symmetric role of $r, c$ in $U_\alpha(r,c)$.

nodes.name: Glue optimal plans via Lemma 1
nodes.statement: Let $P \in U_\alpha(x,y)$ and $Q \in U_\alpha(y,z)$ be the optimal plans for $d_{M,\alpha}(x,y)$ and $d_{M,\alpha}(y,z)$. Apply Lemma 1 to obtain $S \in U_\alpha(x,z)$.

nodes.name: Bound $\langle S, M\rangle$ via triangle inequality on $M$
nodes.statement: $d_{M,\alpha}(x,z) \leq \langle S, M\rangle = \sum_{ik} m_{ik} \sum_j p_{ij}q_{jk}/y_j \leq \sum_{ijk} (m_{ij}+m_{jk}) p_{ij} q_{jk}/y_j$ using $m_{ik} \leq m_{ij}+m_{jk}$.

nodes.name: Marginalize and conclude
nodes.statement: Splitting the sum and using $\sum_k q_{jk}/y_j = 1$ and $\sum_i p_{ij}/y_j = 1$ collapses the bound to $\sum_{ij} m_{ij} p_{ij} + \sum_{jk} m_{jk} q_{jk} = d_{M,\alpha}(x,y) + d_{M,\alpha}(y,z)$.

nodes.name: Define the gluing distribution $T$
nodes.statement: Let $T$ be the joint on $\{1,\ldots,d\}^3$ with $t_{ijk} \defeq p_{ij}q_{jk}/y_j$ for $y_j>0$ (and $t_{ijk} = 0$ otherwise).

nodes.name: Verify row and column sums of $S$
nodes.statement: Set $S = [\sum_j t_{ijk}]_{ik}$. Computing $\sum_i \sum_j s_{ijk}$ telescopes to $\sum_j q_{jk} = z_k$ (column sums) and $\sum_k \sum_j s_{ijk}$ telescopes to $\sum_j p_{ij} = x_i$ (row sums), so $S$ is a transportation matrix between $x$ and $z$.

nodes.name: Entropy bound via data-processing inequality
nodes.statement: Since $p(X,Y,Z) = p(X)p(Y\mid X)p(Z\mid Y)$, $(X,Y,Z)$ is a Markov chain, so the data-processing inequality $I(X;Y) \geq I(X;Z)$ yields $h(X,Z) - h(X) - h(Z) \geq -\alpha$, i.e. $h(S) \geq h(x)+h(z)-\alpha$.

nodes.name: Reduce $U_0(r,c)$ to the singleton $\{rc^T\}$
nodes.statement: $U_0(r,c)$ contains all $P$ with $h(P) = h(r)+h(c)$; by Cover & Thomas Theorem 2.6.6 this forces $P = rc^T$, so $d_{M,0}(r,c) = \langle rc^T, M\rangle = r^T M c$.

nodes.name: Expand $r^T M c$ via Euclidean embedding
nodes.statement: Since $M$ is a Euclidean distance matrix, $m_{ij} = \|\varphi_i - \varphi_j\|^2$. Expanding gives $r^T M c = r^T u + c^T u - 2\, r^T K c$ with $u_i = \|\varphi_i\|^2$ and $K_{ij} = \langle \varphi_i, \varphi_j\rangle$, using $\sum r_i = \sum c_i = 1$.

nodes.name: Show $r^T M c$ is a negative-definite kernel
nodes.statement: $r^T u + c^T u$ is a sum of n.d. kernels (separable), and $-2 r^T K c$ is n.d. as the negative of a positive-definite kernel; their sum $r^T M c$ is therefore negative-definite.
